personagens.resumo: Jodio Joestar (ジョディオ・ジョースター, Jodio Jōsutā) is the protagonist of the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands, and the ninth JoJo of the series.

ja_kanji.texto: ジョディオ・ジョースター

namesake.texto: JoJo (Protagonists) | Dio (Parts 1 & 3 Antagonist)

family.texto: Joseph Joestar (Grandfather) | Suzi Q (Grandmother) | Barbara Ann Joestar (Mother) | Unnamed Father | Holy Joestar-Kira (Aunt) | Dragona Joestar (Older Brother)See: Joestar Family

Appearance: Jodio is a 15-year-old boy. He has light skin and light-colored hair; which has a zig-zag patterning or layering to it, with the top of his hair sometimes depicted as a darker shade or a completely different color to the lower half; with long jagged bangs partially obscuring both of his eyes and an undercut at the back. His hair is asymmetrical, as the right side is braided with a star-shaped ornamental hair clip attached, and the left side is cut just below his eye. He wears a large "JO" shaped earring that hangs from his left ear. As a descendant of the Joestar family, Jodio has the Star Birthmark on his left shoulder; the skin beneath his birthmark is slightly discolored due to a scar from a gunshot wound inflicted by his brother's ex-boyfriend.

His outfit consists of a light short-sleeved shirt under dark hooded overalls with a winged heart emblem at the center of the chest. The emblem is marked by an hourglass symbol with both triangles split into a dark and a bright half, and the shirt has been shown to have the word "NOVEMBER" written on the front collar. The overalls bears a strong resemblance to a life preserver, having a belt fastened around the chest under the heart emblem, sporting rigid light-colored shoulder pads, and exposing most of Jodio's back. The overalls are also fastened to the shirt by two buttons at the back of the waist. The overalls' pantlegs are split under the knee, giving them a similar appearance to bell-bottoms, both also studded in a vertical column besides the slit.

For accessories, Jodio wears assorted fingerless gloves, the main pair consisting of simple wristbands with a triangular flap over the back of the hand. He also has armbands shaped like two triangles wrapped around each bicep. Jodio wears dark plain dress shoes.

As an eleven year old, Jodio wore almost the exact same style of clothing. Rather than the heart emblem, his hoodie had "JO" written in large centered letters with the top line of the J being elongated.
Color Schemes
Personality: Jodio Joestar is an ambitious hoodlum living a life of petty crime in Hawaii who was diagnosed with antisocial personality disorder by his school's psychological test. Despite his aversion to friendship, Jodio is popular at his school and grows to like Meryl Mei Qi's crew, but this relationship is based on "money more than friendship." Unlike previous series protagonists, Jodio has little to no ethical qualms, and author Hirohiko Araki describes him as a "scumbag."

Jodio values his family above all else and becomes erratic if they are ever threatened or mocked. When an eleven-year-old Jodio witnessed a group of classmates harassing Dragona, he "handled" the problem by setting an entire school bus full of students on fire to hurt them. Jodio felt no guilt for starting the fire, but the absurdity of his family's later dissolution perplexed him. The event was formative for both his relationship with Dragona and their adolescence. Soon after, they began working as gofers to financially support and protect their mother.

Dragona notes that Jodio rarely shows emotion in daily life, speaks little, and avoids standing out. Rather than being shy or intimidated, he appears detached from other people, often staring off into the distance as if they do not matter to him. Jodio also tends to be unaware of, and apathetic toward, how to react when confronted with displays of emotion from others, usually observing passively unless prompted to interact by someone else. When Usagi bursts into tears out of concern for his family, Jodio only watches and is surprised when Dragona tells him to comfort him. Whenever his mother cried out of anger after her husband left home, Jodio would simply lean against her while silently staring at Dragona.

He occasionally whispers his thoughts to Dragona, making Dragona speak on his behalf. He typically does this when he needs to communicate with the group outside of battle. While in conflict, he sometimes whispers to others in his gang to relay information, plans, and strategies without alerting the enemy. Howler even threatens Jodio at gunpoint to stop him from whispering because of the paranoia it invokes.

Jodio's general aversion to socialization is disregarded when he wants something from another person. This most commonly happens when he is coordinating a drug deal, but it appears in other situations as well. His entire demeanor quickly shifts to become friendly and cajoling, when moments earlier he would have been suspicious or even outwardly violent. He also tends to address people with familiar or socially accommodating terms, such as calling Usagi "senpai", the undercover cop "sis", and Rohan Kishibe "sensei". He usually stops using these terms after he gets what he wants, with Rohan being the only exception.

Jodio's sole aspiration is wealth, and contrary to his mother's hopes, he performs the worst in his class. Ever since he started out as a gofer, Jodio has approached his "work" with professional diligence and garnered enough notoriety to earn recognition in Hawaii. His upbringing in poverty influenced his outlook, to the point of inspiring his belief in "mechanisms". "Mechanisms" are a set of abstract rules that dictate the distribution of power and wealth in society. For example, Jodio cultivates respect, admiration, and protection through his popularity, whereas a bullied classmate does not.

According to Lulu, even though Jodio looks so young, he gives off the impression of being in charge. In tense situations, he remains composed and in control, giving Dragona or his allies precise instructions. With faith in the Lava Rock's mechanisms, Jodio does not falter when threatened, and Howler also notes that he began acting like the leader of their group at some point during their negotiation. When he decides to act, he moves toward his goal in a quiet, unhurried manner that becomes even more restrained when he faces insults or setbacks. However, Jodio acquiesces to Dragona without question when it comes to deciding their goals, remaining largely apathetic about what they choose. In this way, Jodio acts very differently in battle than he does outside of one, taking more of a leadership role from the shadows during combat while remaining passive toward Dragona's judgment outside of it.

Despite his outwardly calm and level-headed personality, it is suggested that Jodio harbours a lot of rage inside him. This rage stems from his difficult life where he had to live through bullying against him and Dragona as well as the financial hardships his family had gone through, which incurred even more scorn and mockery, something which Jodio takes particularly badly. Point Blank Seal taunts Jodio by reminding him of how unfair society and the legal system is because a man who shot him from behind was judged as not guilty and that such incidents, which Jodio cannot accept, fill him with rage. One time, his vindictiveness from witnessing Dragona's classmates bullying them led to Jodio almost murdering the entire class by burning the bus in which they were in. Jodio qualifies the unfairness of life as "absurdities".
Jodio loves Rohan Kishibe's work, Pink Dark Boy, listens to music, and often plays with a handheld gaming console.
Jodio openly claims to be really bad at remembering three-letter acronyms.
According to Point Blank Seal, Jodio exhibits all three characteristics of the Macdonald triad.
Abilities: Stand

Jodio wields November Rain, a Stand that is able to create localized showers of rain in a 3 meter radius by 4 meter height that can selectively become heavy enough to redirect bullets, destroy concrete, or punch through the steel hull of a ship.

Jodio is able to control the degree of force the rain exerts by modifying its gravitational force. November Rain's range only limits where rain can be generated, so Jodio is able to control the rain's weight from any distance. Jodio uses this to create traps using the rainwater, as he did to capture Rohan.

personagens.resumo: Dragona Joestar (ドラゴナ・ジョースター, Doragona Jōsutā) is a primary ally featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: ドラゴナ・ジョースター

alias.texto: Pink-chan (ピンクちゃんPinku-chanPinku-chan) (Code name by Usagi) | Pink Nagasaki (ピンク・ナガサキPinku NagasakiPinku Nagasaki)

namesake.texto: Dragona ("Dragoness" in Spanish) | Nagasaki, Nagasaki Prefecture, Japan (Japanese city) (Alias)

family.texto: Joseph Joestar (Grandfather) | Suzi Q (Grandmother) | Barbara Ann Joestar (Mother) | Unnamed Father | Holy Joestar-Kira (Aunt) | Jodio Joestar (Younger Brother) | Unnamed Ex-BoyfriendSee: Joestar Family

Appearance: Dragona is a slim 18 year-old with a feminine figure, dark skin, shoulder-length locs, and long eyelashes. Dragona wears a crown of flowers, some having elongated petals that are reminiscent of hands, with a few locs swept over the crown as bangs. As a descendant of the Joestar family, Dragona's left shoulder has the Star Birthmark.

The outfits Dragona wears are typically feminine, such as two-piece bikinis and dresses. There are stylized dragon tattoos on Dragona's shoulders and left thigh, and triple claw-like tattoos on the chest, arms, and left thigh. According to Jodio, the slight swelling in Dragona's chest is from cosmetic injections.

Dragona consistently wears a few accessories, those being arm and wrist bracelets, and a chest pendant engraved with a stylized "D" made to look like a dragon. The pendant also has a pocket on the back. Dragona's main outfit consists of a sleeveless one-piece romper with a shirt collar, a serrated hem and a buttoned pouch in the place of a back pocket. When going on heists, Dragona's facemask is rolled over the collar like a scarf, with a few locs tucked under it.

As a fourteen-year-old, Dragona had a short shag hairstyle. One outfit at school was a light collared sleeveless shirt with a few buttons and the dragon-stylized "D" below the left shoulder. Dragona wore it alongside light shorts and dark sneakers. A few months later, Dragona began wearing more feminine attire, composed of a light tanktop with dark straps, the "D" chest pendant, a headband with a few flowers, a belt with a "JO" accessory, and light pants.
Color Schemes
Personality: Dragona is a jovial, amiable, and active person, who participates in various crimes alongside younger brother Jodio for the sake of supporting their family. Resilience, introspection, and protectiveness toward Jodio characterize Dragona. As a fan of girly fashion, Dragona dresses in feminine outfits, and uses the Japanese first-person pronoun "atashi" (あたし), which is primarily used by women.

As a fourteen-year-old, Dragona was bullied, harassed, and assaulted by a female classmate who took advantage of Dragona's meek disposition. The bully mocked Dragona's appearance by taunting that a bra should be worn, and that the Joestar siblings should call each other sisters rather than brothers. Although Dragona minimized the severity of the bullying and dismissed it as the classmate just joking, the assault led to nightmares and Dragona struggled to sleep. Jodio's decision to take matters into his own hands by burning Dragona's classmates led Dragona to strive to become stronger, admitting that if the bullying had continued before Jodio ended up doing that, it would have been a soul-crushing experience from which recovery would have been impossible. Growing up, Dragona moves on from the trauma by framing the incident as a random absurd event in life. While still considering it as an extremely important moment despite having no responsibility for it occurring, Dragona believes that not letting it go is equivalent to accepting emotional ruin.

Dragona tends to act as the cautious one among the team, warning them whenever they go too far. Dragona is more inclined to resolve situations through conversation or at least use guile and surprise attacks instead of rushing head first into conflicts. Dragona disapproves when Jodio resorts to extreme violence like setting the school bus on fire or needlessly stomping on a police officer, though nonetheless feels relief and thanks Jodio afterward as Jodio would be doing those things for Dragona's sake. Despite living a criminal life, Dragona also treats the legitimate job at the fashion boutique seriously and heavily objects to fellow gangster Paco stealing from the clients, scolding him and even pulling his ear to punish him. Unlike Paco and Usagi, Dragona acts warily while searching for the diamond in Rohan's villa, berating the two for stealing things they don't need. Being goal-oriented, Dragona rejects Usagi's confession of love, stating that neither Dragona nor Jodio are interested in such matters.

Dragona is physically active, jogging every morning and following yoga courses. Dragona's motto, which was picked up from an Indian yoga instructor, is to "never push yourself too hard, but never give up either," indicating a preference for steady effort. Papaya is a favorite food and the only thing Dragona eats for breakfast. Dragona acts like the parent of Smooth Operators, referring to the Stand as kids.
Abilities: Stand

Dragona wields Smooth Operators, a Multi-Unit Stand comprised of four small units on tank treads that can grab and shift physical features along a two-dimensional plane. By "sliding" a surface, they can displace fixed details ranging from printed numbers on an object to physical wounds on a body.

personagens.resumo: Paco Laburantes (パコ・ラブランテス, Pako Raburantesu) is a primary ally featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: Paco Rabanne (Spanish-French fashion designer) | Laburantes ("Workers" in Rioplatense Spanish)

occupation.texto: Student | Port Warehouse Manager | United States Military (Dishonarably discharged) | Gofer

Appearance: Paco is a 19-year-old teenager with an athletic build. Despite his youth, he has rugged features making him look more mature. A piece of his left ear is chewed off. Jodio notes that Paco used to be sort of chubby, but lost weight and became more muscular when he was around 17. However, he is shown to have still been muscular as a child and young teenager. He has light hair that goes down to his neck, finishing in a square cut. His hair is mostly covered by his cap, which bears a stylized plate with "P∆CO" engraved on it. Paco has distinctive dark tattoo-like marks and spots covering his freckles below his eyes that extend vertically to his chin. He also has a chain of triangles split into dark and bright halves tattooed along his arms from his hands up to his shoulders.

Paco wears a harness comprised of two wide straps with several grommets that cross each other over his solar plexus. There is a hood attached by the two grommets over his shoulders. On the strap crossing over his right pectoral is a large brooch-like object resembling a melting ice cream cone stylized to spell out his name "PACO". He also wears plain trousers with "P∆CO" engraved on the belt buckle, as well as several straps at the waist and knee pads. Finally, he wears sneakers, wristbands and, in earlier appearances, a necklace. Later on, he is also shown wearing a codpiece. He wears a smartwatch underneath his left wristband. Paco states that his top and boots cost $2000.

When Paco was a child and later around 14 years old, he wore the same hat, a T-shirt, wristbands, the same belt, and pants with "P" and "C" printed on the knee areas. He lacked the tattoos on his face and arms, having visible freckles below his eyes instead. After getting out of prison, he replaced the "P" and "C" with knee pads.
Color Schemes
Personality: Paco Laburantes is a loud, straightforward teenager, whose personality was shaped by his rough upbringing. His father was a violent alcoholic who frequently beat him over minor grievances, while his mother abandoned the family and never returned. Paco is quick to openly speak his mind, making him come across as rude or ill-mannered. He develops a particular fondness for Jodio and Dragona, while making sarcastic remarks to Usagi or telling him to shut up. Paco is recognized for his skills as a kleptomaniac. Although he began committing crimes to earn enough money to hire a lawyer for his father, his thrill for theft is described by Jodio as almost "game-like", leading him frequently into trouble. Thus, Barbara Ann Joestar doesn't want Jodio associating with him because of the rumors she's heard, believing that he's the type to intimidate kids that he has power over.

Paco is quite brutish, threatening to get violent when he doesn't get his way, and confidently admitting that violence is his area of expertise. While trying to find Charming Man after he got away with the Lava Rock, Paco strangles ordinary bystanders like Leo to see if their skin has the same sandy texture. His speech is notable for the use of child-like words where he duplicates syllables, such as "ouchi" (おうち)[b] for "home" and "otete" (お手手)[c] for "hand".

Paco is observant and judgmental, often recognizing both positive and negative characteristics of others. He immediately suspects Usagi of being a drug addict and frequently critiques Charming Man's poor knife-wielding skills. Despite his rough exterior and sometimes criticizing his allies, Paco demonstrates emotional maturity and empathy. Although he sees his relationship with his teammates as a business arrangement rather than a genuine friendship, he values his allies and those he deems good. For instance, when he senses that Charming Man is actually a good person, Paco recalculates his stance on killing him, understanding that teaming up would lead to a win-win situation. When Usagi has an emotional breakdown over Meryl Mei Qi's abduction, Paco comforts him by patting him and validating his feelings, telling him there's no shame in backing out and that he promises to still give Usagi a smaller share of Hacca Howler's assets if he chooses not to go further with their mission. He warns Usagi of the danger and long-term consequences of confronting the police at the boutique, showing concern for his future and reassuring him that he will make friends eventually.

Paco demonstrates leadership qualities such as discussing strategies with his teammates, studying maps of their heist locations, delegating tasks, giving orders, and making decisions for the gang. For instance, Paco determines when they should return to the airport or head out on their missions, decides for the whole team that Charming Man should be their ally, and orders Dragona to submit the authorization on Congressman White's tablet. When Usagi decides to continue with the mission of rescuing Meryl Mei, Paco outlines their next steps and allows him to carry a concealed gun. Paco is also always the driver of the vehicles on the team's missions. He is aware of his surroundings and quick to react to sudden enemy attacks, using The Hustle on Jodio's neck to protect him from Charming Man's attack, and warning Dragona not to touch the watch that was seemingly flying toward them.

Paco's impulsivity can contrast against his leadership, at times leading him to be unpredictable when he interacts with enemies and allies alike, such as him deciding to recruit Charming Man when minutes before he was vowing to kill him.

Despite this, when innocent people or his allies are in danger, he always protects them. Examples of this would be taking bullets for Dragona's safety in the fight with Bobby Jean, and jumping into the crocodile enclosure to help Usagi. When Paco failed to rescue a child, he felt immense guilt for not being strong enough, saying over and over that he didn't mean to let go of him. A potential explanation for his extreme devastation is revealed when he was targeted by Point Blank Seal. As part of the Stand's abilities, it targets the insecurities of its victim. For Paco, it taunted him about how his mother abandoned him and his father, and anticipated that he will abandon others just like she did. From this, it is implied that Paco's dedication to his allies and innocents is at least partially rooted in his trauma regarding being abandoned by his mother as a child. His abandonment insecurities surfaced when he thought that Usagi had abandoned them, anxiously claiming that he was going to kill him whenever he saw him again and then he was moved to tears when he saw that Usagi came back to help them and did not plan on abandoning them
Abilities: Stand
Paco's Stand The Hustle allows him to freely manipulate his muscles, notably allowing him to bulge his muscles to grab objects and attach them to his skin.
Hand-to-Hand Combat

Paco shows he is proficient at hand-to-hand combat when he fights and fends off Charming Man for a moment. During their fight, he skillfully blocks and evades the enemy's dagger strikes, even managing to take an advantage and grab him.
Military Training
Prior to working for Meryl Mei Qi, Paco had enlisted in the U.S. Military but was dishonorably discharged.

personagens.resumo: Usagi Alohaoe (ウサギ・アロハオエ, Usagi Arohaoe) is a primary ally featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: Usagi (ウサギ) ("Rabbit" in Japanese) | Aloha ʻOe (Hawaiian folk song written by Queen Liliʻuokalani, later covered by Elvis Presley for Blue Hawaii)

family.texto: Alison Alohaoe (Mother) | Unnamed Father | Tory Alohaoe (Younger Sister)

Appearance: Usagi is a slim, well-toned, athletic teenager. He wears a tight form-fitting dark suit that covers most of his body aside from the face and hands. He has a few light-colored spiky bangs protruding from under the hood of his suit, which is tight enough to show that he has a short standard haircut save for the bangs and a small ponytail, which is covered by his hood.
Usagi has an upturned nose, dark eyes and big lips which stand out when he expresses surprise.

His suit is noticeably darker near the stomach. In addition, the suit is decorated with circular crests at the shoulders. Initially, the crests displayed art resembling legs wearing a garter belt, but the symbol was later flipped upside down, now resembling legs in simple panties and high heels, as well as the outstretched arms of his Stand.

Over his suit, Usagi wears a pair of light shorts with a thick stripe, as well as a backpack. Usagi's accessories include a light-colored beret and a black choker with a small buckle, although his initial appearance didn't feature them. Usagi also wears thick eyeliner.
Color Schemes
Personality: Usagi Alohaoe is scatterbrained, tardy, and hedonistic, but he is still trusted by Meryl Mei Qi to accompany her crew. Acting as the "airhead" of the group, Usagi often disregards simple instructions and is easily distracted by food and money. He has a habit of showing up with food ready to eat even in inappropriate situations. Before the mission to acquire HOWLER's land deeds, Meryl stresses the importance of leaving no trace or witness behind. Characteristically, Usagi trips and spills food all over the floor of the land registry in front of several armed guards, which later allows Lulu and Bobby Jean to track down his team. His behavior initially causes Jodio and the others to distrust him, though they eventually come to see him as useful, trying to save his life from Bags' Groove's attack and later helping him search for his missing mother and younger sister.

Though the group often chides Usagi, he remains friendly toward all of them to a comical degree. He is especially fond of Dragona, calling them "Pink-chan" and confessing his love for them after knowing each other for only three days. Although he is amiable with his crew, Usagi is still a sleazy teenager and swindles them by pretending their rental car cost more than it actually did so he would not have to pay for it.

Usagi is also fairly inquisitive and manages to ascertain the basic properties of the Lava Rock by experimenting with it. He is comparatively more educated than the rest of Meryl's crew, and Meryl herself states that he is an accomplished student. For example, he explains to Paco and Dragona the difference between flasks and beakers, as well as what 'a'ā lava is. He also knows of different endangered bird species in the jungle, and devises a clever plan to save the crew during their encounter with Wild Cat Size by serving them caviar to attract them to the Lava Rock. He is usually the first in the gang to realize when they are being attacked by a Stand and who the user may be, but his gangmates typically do not believe him until they see further proof.

Usagi is highly emotional and dramatic, often crying when he or his teammates are injured. At the same time, he can be brave and decisive in a crisis, as shown when he saves his own life by unhesitatingly piercing his chest with a box cutter so that he can use a straw to perform tracheal intubation. This emotional side becomes even more pronounced when his family is endangered. After learning that his family's bank account has been emptied and that his mother Alison and sister Tory have disappeared, he becomes visibly distressed and unusually confrontational. He angrily demands answers from Meryl Mei Qi about the delayed payout from the Hualalai north slope deal, forcing Paco to momentarily render him unconscious before he would go look for his family alone. Once Usagi learns that the case may involve cyber fraud and a legal agreement concerning Tory's organs, his anger quickly gives way to panic and desperation. During the search for his family, he cries, shouts, and refuses to back down even after discovering Max's corpse in the house where his mother and sister were last seen on security cameras.
Usagi is bisexual, having developed a crush on a male friend from another school when he was 14, though he also likes girls.
Usagi is a client of Jodio and bought drugs from him prior to his recruitment. He later admits that although he experimented with drugs two or three times in the past, he is not an addict.
Abilities: Stand
Usagi's Stand THE MATTEKUDASAI can transform into objects that others around Usagi request.

personagens.resumo: Charming Man (チャーミング・マン, Chāmingu Man) is a primary ally featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: This Charming Man (The Smiths song)

goals.texto: Retrieve the Lava Rock from Jodio Joestar (Formerly) | Find his missing brother

mangadebut.texto: TJL Chapter 8 (Disguised) | TJL Chapter 10 (1st full debut)

Appearance: Charming Man is a 21-year-old man with an athletic build, and dark, spiky, shoulder-length hair. His hair is flat at the top with spiky bangs, and the back of his hair juts out in all directions. Charming Man wears makeup, including eye shadows and dark lipstick. He has distinct vertical face markings that run down from his lower eyelids to just above his jawline.

His outfit consists of a sleeveless jumpsuit with shoulder straps that connect to an upward-facing triangle at the back, and he has a large bow tie on his chest. The shoulder straps have a dark jagged pattern with triangles pointing outward. There are oval-shaped lace-like decorations of varying sizes on his chest behind his jumpsuit and bow tie. In addition, Charming Man wears dark wristbands, knee pads, and sneakers. In his first appearance, he has bow ties on his knees instead of the knee pads. In his flashback, he wears a t-shirt underneath his jumpsuit and the shoulder straps also lack the dark jagged pattern. While bicycling, he wears a helmet with a dark visor and has a backpack.

When Charming Man uses his ability, he has numerous sand fragments floating around his face and upper torso. His skin also feels like coarse sand, which has been like that ever since he was born. This trait is apparently shared among the people and animals of his village. Due to his ability, his facial features can change. Charming Man is disguised as Paco Laburantes when he first appears, looking exactly like him. He hides the sand fragments floating around him before revealing his true nature. At first, his irises are light when his disguise as Paco wears off, but they are normally dark afterwards.
Color Schemes
Personality: Charming Man is an energetic and caring elder brother, yet also demanding and aggressive. He is athletic and enjoys participating in recreational activities such as bicycle races and 2-mile swimming marathons with his younger brother. He looks forward to those events with excitement and has a competitive spirit. He gains an interest in the Lava Rock after his younger brother falls into a lava tube where the Lava Rock came from. However, he doesn't desire it for money since he thinks that it's impossible to become rich using it. Rather, he thinks using it would help him find his younger brother.

Charming Man resorts to violence when he doesn't get his way, using brutal methods such as siccing Wild Cat Size onto Jodio and his friends to strangle them when they steal Rohan's diamond and Lava Rock. He also has no qualms about trying to murder them himself, nearly slashing Jodio's throat and stabbing Dragona in the neck. Charming Man is manipulative and cunning, since he attempts to psychologically persuade Jodio into handing over the Lava Rock. He aims to scare Jodio into thinking the mafia might be after him and his friends, and shows an illusion of his cats' decapitated heads inside Jodio's food bag. Moreover, he intelligently uses his environment to trick his opponents.

He has a bad reputation among the local police officers on the island of Hawaii, who make excuses so they don't have to help him find his brother. They place the blame on him instead, bringing up unrelated issues such as an argument he had with Mauka on the previous day and his arrest record from injuring a police officer. Nonetheless, their accusations aren't completely his fault, as the officer just scraped his palm against Charming Man's rough skin after stopping him for a traffic violation. Charming Man is also somewhat merciful as he gives Jodio a chance to return the Lava Rock first before personally attacking him. Despite trying to kill them, Paco believes that he is actually a good person and chooses to make him their ally. He doesn't consider Rohan an enemy and easily becomes cooperative with the gang when they suggest to work together, willingly answering any of their questions. However, it is possible that he didn't give his real name to them, as Paco wonders whether "Charming Man" is actually a name.

Charming Man doesn't tolerate drug addicts, declaring that "100% of junkies are liars". Assuming that Usagi is a drug addict, he suggests to Dragona that they should abandon him after he suffers from a pulmonary edema. On the other hand, he has respect for people who take things on alone, and changes his mind about Usagi upon seeing his bravery.
He enjoys listening to Sia, H.E.R., and SZA, though admits he tends to mix up their names.
Abilities: Stand

Big Mouth Strikes Again manifests as sand-like skin particles, allowing Charming Man to alter the perceptions of his enemies by camouflaging with his surroundings and creating fake disguises. This also allows him to impersonate another person using another layer of sand-like skin. It's possible to hide objects under the disguised skin, such as a knife. The disguise can also be destroyed with enough force, such as Jodio's heavy rain.
Personal Skills
Bicycle Riding: Charming Man is a skilled bicyclist who can do bunny hops to dodge fallen trees.

Knife Proficiency: Charming Man fights with a knife he carries with him, frequently swinging it around. He is more adept at using it for surprise attacks than for hand-to-hand combat, as Paco is easily able to dodge and counter his attacks. Paco also notes that his skills with a knife aren't good enough for him to be an assassin.
Physical Disposition

According to himself, Charming Man possesses several beneficial natural traits. His family members and villagers are able to easily bear with the heat and cold, and have long life spans. However, the primary cause of death for the members of his village in old age is the calcification of waste products.

personagens.resumo: Meryl Mei Qi (メリル・メイ・チー, Meriru Mei Chī) is a secondary ally featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

occupation.texto: High School Principal | IKO IKO Boutique Proprietress | Gang Boss | Housewife

Appearance: Meryl Mei is an imposingly tall, plump woman. She towers over the people around her, being two heads taller than Dragona and being nearly level with the doorway to IKO IKO. She has medium colored chin length hair which she wears tied into a blunt ponytail.

Meryl Mei wears a long, loose dress similar to a muumuu. It is split at the waist, has a leaf motif, and is decorated with fringes at the hips. She also has shoulder bows, loafers decorated with bow ties, and plain stud earrings. She later wears a pearl necklace.
After the nine month timeskip, she wears high heels and pearl anklets that match with her necklace.
Color Schemes
Personality: Meryl Mei Qi is considered a "superwoman" by Jodio Joestar, leading a triple life as an educator, talented fashion designer, and criminal mastermind. Under her facade as a well-loved and respectable public figure, she is actually a meticulous crime boss. Meryl Mei is publicly known as a high school principal, where she is loved by the students, all of whom gladly salute her and whom she greets in return. She is also the owner of IKO IKO, a fashion boutique in Kalihi. She personally works on many aspects of the boutique, such as designing the clothing, merchandise, and posters; Jodio admires her work and judges that she could be a successful fashion designer even in Paris or Milan if she ever put her mind to it.

As a crime boss, her office at IKO IKO is her base where she hands out missions to her members. Beneath her cheerful act as a principal is a woman with ulterior motives who doesn't truly care about her students, recruiting young children to risk their lives doing illegal acts for her like robberies or smuggling goods. She is very cautious and does not want to leave any trace of her felonies. For instance, she tells her underlings to shut down their cell phones when discussing their crimes, and hides her address from them. Her shop is also a front to hide the income from her criminal business. She is well connected, having spies and acquaintances working as customs officers at the local international airports, hotels, newspaper companies, and even the police department. She also has ties with the black market to be able to sell a precious diamond. Meryl Mei occasionally advises her subordinates to expand their drug sales to university students and such, because she doesn't wish for her business to be completely closed off.

The two sides of her seem to have more overlap in personality than would initially seem, as she treats her underlings like elementary schoolers despite them being teenagers or young adults. She always claps her hands and sings her order for them to shut down their phones, though her team happily claps and sings back. She can be perceptive and intimidating, as she realizes when her gang members are hiding something from her and then demands that they tell her the truth.

Despite her wealth, she is manipulative and greedy, always wanting to make even greater gains. For example, she admits to Jodio and Dragona that she wouldn't have invited them into her gang if they wouldn't make her a profit. Nonetheless, her underlings are grateful for her recruitment, and see that as her saving them from misfortune. Usagi in particular views her as the only person who cared about him when no one else would.

personagens.resumo: Rohan Kishibe (岸辺 露伴, Kishibe Rohan) is a secondary ally featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: Rohan Kishibe (Part 4 character) | Rohan Koda (Meiji-era author)

residence.texto: Rohan's House, Morioh | Rohan's Villa, Hawaii (Temporary)

etymology.texto: 岸 (Kishi) = Beach | 辺 (Be) = Boundary/environs | 露 (Ro) = Ephemereal | 伴 (Han) = To be with

mangadebut.texto: TJL Chapter 1 (1st mentioned) | TJL Chapter 2 (1st full debut)

Appearance: Rohan is an adult with a muscular build and average height. His hair is slicked sideways with an undercut. He wears a headband with serrated edges and earrings designed to look like pen tips. Rohan's outfit in Hawaii consists of a button shirt, shorts, and sandals. His shoulders, the sides of his shorts, and his wristbands also have pen tips stitched on. He very closely resembles his counterpart from the original continuity.
Color Schemes
Personality: Rohan Kishibe is an inquisitive and passionate manga artist dedicated to his work. To gain inspiration, Rohan is constantly seeking new experiences or facts, investigating anything regardless of the danger or legality. For instance, he explores a volcanic area, takes detailed photos, and brings back samples of cooled lava with him despite the area being forbidden to tourists. He is easily able to discern when something appears suspicious, such as when he wonders about the cat at his house, as well as how the rain only targeted a specific spot.
In addition to his own work, Rohan pursues art in all its forms. At his villa, he possesses a notable amount of statues, antiques, and bottles of alcohol.

Rohan is laid-back and unflustered even when he is outnumbered by the gang robbing his house. Despite the four of them being Stand users, Rohan remains calm and easily handles them, even warning them of the dangers should they continue to try stealing the diamond.
Abilities: Stand

Heaven's Door enables Rohan to transmute people into "human books", with written pages unfurling from their bodies. These pages allow Rohan to learn detailed information about that person, including biological characteristics, history, personality, or even details of their Stand and its abilities.

personagens.resumo: Hacca Howler (アッカ・ハウラー, Akka Haurā) is the main antagonist of the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands, as well as the eighth main antagonist of the series overall.

namesake.texto: Hacca (Alternative form of the letter "H" in Italian) | The Howler (King Crimson song)

family.texto: Latrato (7th Generation Ancestor) | Unnamed Ancestress (7th Generation Ancestress) | Unnamed Grandfather | Lulu (Daughter, presumed by Lulu)See: Howler Family

mangadebut.texto: TJL Chapter 16 (Mentioned)Mentioned only | TJL Chapter 17 (1st full debut)

Appearance: Howler is a man with an athletic build and a young looking face. He has shoulder-length hair that is tied back. His hair is voluminous at the top styled in a jelly roll or elephant trunk, albeit with the front gap similar to a heart shape rather than a circle. Howler's beard looks like rectangular strips with gaps in between, going from the sides of his ears to his chin. The top strips of the beard are longer and angled toward his eyes.

He wears a light short sleeve shirt with notch collars, slightly exposing his upper chest. The shirt has a thick dark outline running down vertically from his collars to above the edge of his shirt, with the lines connecting horizontally at the back. His sleeves also have a dark line going across above the edge. He pairs the shirt with light shorts that have checkered hems.
Below his clothes, Howler wears a mesh bodysuit that is dark and semi-transparent with several circular holes. It has long sleeves and covers his arms and legs.

In addition, Howler wears a choker on his neck made of several "H"-shaped emblems, has an "h" emblem shaped like a wolf from his company's logo embedded on his shirt near his abdomen, dark wristbands, and dark sneakers with light shoelaces and edges.
As a teenager, his hair was a bit shorter, not needing to be tied. He also slicked back his bangs.
Color Schemes
Personality: Hacca Howler is a narcissistic businessman who indulges in a luxurious lifestyle, frequently flaunting his wealth and power. He takes pride in his family's legacy, refusing to surrender the land on the Hualalai north slope he inherited from his ancestor. He favors top-quality goods, knowing which areas of Hokkaido produce the best kombu and claiming he rides only in Rolls-Royce with the starlight headliner when being picked up or dropped off from airports. Howler is often shown in the company of women, pursuing pleasure by being flirtatious and promiscuous: as a teenager, he invites a girl into the bathtub at his grandfather's house; years later, Lulu suggests he may be her father; he dotes on three flight attendants on his private jet, feeding them as they lie in his lap and kissing them goodbye; and he is shown relaxing with another woman in his car.

Howler openly acts unethically, believing that his wealth could solve any problem, and admitting that his own actions of committing land fraud are villainous. He treats affection as something money can purchase, boasting that he could "buy all of Hokkaido" for his flight attendants and arguing that the environment would be protected better if he bought the land, despite wanting to build resorts on it. Later, he attempts to bribe the fake Dolphin Bank employees with $40 million each to erase his $30 billion debt.

Howler is mistrustful of others and has an explosive temper, especially when he is inconvenienced. He acts condescendingly to even his acquaintances and employees. For example, he rudely demands that Yokohama and the Dolphin Bank employees leave from his private immigration gate so that he could enter Hawaii, and constantly tells Key West to do her job. When his driver is forced to stop on the road due to protesters, Howler furiously fires him on the spot and immediately calls to have the entire public road purchased to make it his private property. He is openly contemptuous of the public and reporters, barking at his company's protesters to get out of his way. As the leader of the HOWLER company, he is authoritative and expects unquestioning loyalty, ordering his employees to find the missing Lulu while refusing to give them any context about what Bobby Jean was investigating. He is quick to resort to threats and violence, fine with murdering anyone who gets in the way of his wealth. During his business negotiation, he points a gun at everyone to intimidate them, including Key West, and promises to throw anyone who fails to give him a satisfactory answer into the open sea.

His composure falters under stress, with Laem Chabang calling him out for being afraid and Key West advising him to be more imposing. He panics upon learning that someone brought a Lava Rock onto his yacht, frantically searching for it and worrying about his downfall. This paranoia leads to him impulsively shooting the wall behind Jodio after seeing him whisper to Dragona, causing a fire on his own yacht.
Abilities: Stand
Howler wields Eclipse Eight, which has a currently unknown ability. It manifests alongside mist.

personagens.resumo: Lulu (ルルちゃん, Ruru-chan) is a secondary antagonist featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands, specifically the "Lulu's Bags' Groove" and "Lulu and Bobby Jean" story arcs.

family.texto: Hacca Howler (Father, presumed by Lulu) | Unnamed Mother

mangadebut.texto: TJL Chapter 15 (1st mentioned) | TJL Chapter 16 (1st full debut)

Appearance: Lulu is a short girl with thick eyebrows. Her shoulder-length wavy hair is styled with a braided headband that wraps around her head. Her outfit is a sleeveless patchwork dress with multiple jagged pieces of fabric overlapping each other. She also wears dark studded wristbands and shoes.
Color Schemes
Personality: Lulu has a playful and childlike demeanor, while also being very demanding, manipulative, and bossy. She shows enthusiastic expressions and persistently pleads for Bobby Jean to buy anything she finds cute, such as a "Hula NYAN Dancer" figure or a flower hair ornament that Dragona left behind. When begging for something, she acts extremely insistent, akin to a child having a temper tantrum. For example, while demanding for Bobby to buy her the flower ornament, she repeatedly scratches the vehicle in front of her using her hula figure. Lulu acts entitled and tries appealing to Bobby's emotions by crying and suggesting he doesn't care about her if he won't buy her what she wants. She typically elongates her words, such as when she's begging for the figure or calling it cute. When a security guard tells her the figure is no longer for sale, she shows that she is selfish and adamant by rudely dismissing and insulting his aesthetic sense before begging Bobby to buy the figure again. Lulu is also shown to have extravagant tastes, with Meryl Mei Qi noting that she has refused to drink any water that is not San Pellegrino and demanded to be fed fatty marbled wagyu beef, while also mentioning that Lulu has said she dislikes mangoes.

Despite how Lulu looks and occasionally acts, she is pragmatic and intelligent. She quickly changes her attitude upon getting a nosebleed, realizing that her Stand is battling Stand users. She is observant and attentive, easily pointing out inconsistencies in the surveillance footage and discovering that it is fake, deciphering that their targets must have went to the hospital to use an MRI for locating Bags' Groove, and correctly deducing that the silence from upstairs means Ningbo has likely been killed. She also has an indifferent and cynical outlook on life, announcing that it does not matter to her whether they pursue the enemy group or let them go, as everyone would eventually die from an illness or accident either way. In addition, she takes pride in her Stand being able to kill her targets before any doctor could even find the lesions it inflicts. When interrogated and threatened by Laem Chabang, Lulu does not panic. Instead, she employs psychological tactics to turn the tables on her captor. She first feigns ignorance by making small talk and complimenting Laem Chabang's hairstyle before pivoting to questioning Laem's loyalty and attempting to exploit her greed. After revealing her familial relationship with Hacca Howler to shock Laem, she seizes the opportunity to activate Bags' Groove, proving she can patiently wait for the perfect moment to launch a counter-attack.
Abilities: Stand

Bags' Groove is an automatic colony Stand that attacks anyone who touches the objects Lulu has set it up into, such as the original paper copies of HOWLER's land deeds. The Stand can infiltrate the bodies of multiple victims at the same time and travel through their blood vessels, causing internal injuries which lead to disease-like symptoms and conditions such as a pulmonary edema or cancer.

personagens.resumo: Bobby Jean (ボビー・ジーン, Bobī Jīn) is a secondary antagonist featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands, specifically the "Lulu and Bobby Jean" story arc.

alias.texto: Investigator Bobby Jean (ボビー・ジーン捜査官Bobī Jīn-SōsakanBobī Jīn-Sōsakan)

namesake.texto: Bobby Jean (Bruce Springsteen song)

cod.texto: Pierced through the head by November Rain's droplets

Appearance: Bobby Jean is a man with an average height and build. He has sharp facial features with thick, arched eyebrows, thin cheeks, and a mustache. He wears a bucket hat patterned with crosshair symbols all around it. He also has thick, long sideburns and a ponytail.

Bobby's outfit is a tight-fitted long sleeve shirt with long pointed collars and rectangular buttons. It has a ribbed hem and cuffs. The back of his shirt has a graphic print of three flowers. He also wears shorts, knee-high socks, and shoes.
Bobby Jean carries a legally authorized gun and silencer with him, hidden in the back of his shorts. It resembles a USP45 semi-automatic pistol.
Color Schemes
Personality: Bobby Jean is a respected individual working for the HOWLER Company. He is shown to be somewhat private, sly, and blunt. He is not above bribery, as shown with him offering the Land Registry Office guard money in return for a "Hula NYAN Dancer" figure, and pressures him when rejected.

Despite his authority above others, Bobby Jean is bossed around by Lulu and at times pushed to doing her bidding. However, he is actually a disciplined man who values order and proper behavior. He finds Lulu's begging annoying and only fulfills her demands because they're coworkers. He has a firm stance on how children should behave, being quick to point out that he would not tolerate whining or demanding behavior from his own kids or else he'd give them a spanking. Although he has a stern demeanor, Bobby is not entirely without compassion. He attempts to comfort Lulu when she becomes emotional, albeit in a somewhat detached manner, reassuring her that good things will eventually come her way.

In his work, Bobby takes his responsibilities seriously. He ensures that his tasks are completed properly but refuses to do more than what he's paid for. Even if his targets are minors, he doesn't mind killing them in exchange for money, and would shoot them even without having complete proof of them being his targets.
Abilities: Stand
Glory Days is a Stand that is capable of manipulating the muzzle velocity of the firearms he uses — which is the speed at which Bobby Jean's bullets are fired and strike his targets.

personagens.resumo: Key West (キー・ウエスト, Kī Uesuto) is a secondary antagonist featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

alias.texto: Attorney Key West (キー・ウエスト弁護士Kī Uesuto-BengoshiKī Uesuto-Bengoshi)

namesake.texto: Key West, Florida, USA (American island city)

Appearance: Key West is a tall woman with long, dark hair, thick eyebrows, and an athletic build. She wears a uniform consisting of a long-sleeved shirt and a long skirt, her shirt donning a large sun-shaped patch featuring a "W" logo on her chest and five beads in a V-shaped pattern on her chest pockets. She also has a circular patch on her shoulder with a "W" on it. Key wears a structured cap with the word "Key" prominently displayed on the front in a circle. Her outfit is accentuated by a leather belt with large pouches secured at her waist and beneath her skirt she wears dark high-heeled shoes with laces, similar to sneakers.
Color Schemes
Personality: Key West is a cool-headed, assertive attorney who instinctively takes control of tense situations and shields her client's interests when it benefits her. When a mob of protesters surrounds Hacca Howler, she steps between them and Howler, shuts down their accusations with legal warnings, and makes it clear that crossing onto company property will have consequences. She also counsels Howler to project strength and authority, "like a final boss," revealing her belief that authority is partly a performance and that composure deters threats. Despite outwardly appearing loyal to Howler, she coordinates with Laem Chabang in private text messages to seize the Lava Rock for themselves, treating Howler as a means to an end. She lies to Howler about updates while secretly texting Laem, proving that she values money over her client.

Key is pragmatic, skeptical, and quick to interrogate claims that don't add up. During the visit from the fake Dolphin Bank employees, she challenges "Yokohama" on whether he truly has authority to trade land, rather than accepting his story at face value. She frames her work as protecting the HOWLER Company's assets and pushes back on decisions that jeopardize those interests, such as opposing an immediate land-exchange signature. She also argues technical limits with the FBI, asserting that the Howler family chapel isn't for seizure.

She is also tactical and adaptive, quickly accepting that the government agents boarding Howler's yacht cannot be stopped and moves to mitigate risk by getting Howler to step outside. In addition, she deduces the Lava Rock likely transferred from Dragona to Jodio and successfully manages to steal it from them.

Key West is normally socially smooth and can appear friendly. She compliments Dragona's skin and asks where Dragona studied. When Dragona lies about attending Harvard, Key shows excitement to meet a fellow alumni. However, her composure collapses when she suddenly stops receiving messages from Laem Chabang. After Jodio and Dragona's cover is blown, Key West becomes openly contemptuous, calling them "losers" and insulting their parents. She frames them as filth from cracks in society, showing she considers herself superior.
Abilities: Stand
West End Girl materializes and emerges from within gaps, and uses multiple hands to apply crushing pressure.

personagens.resumo: Laem Chabang (レムチャバン, Remu Chaban) is a secondary antagonist featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: Laem Chabang, Chonburi, Thailand (Thai port city)

Appearance: Laem Chabang is a short, dark-skinned woman who is bald aside from a light colored ponytail. Her face has two tattoos above and below her left eye of large swallows with dark and light patterns carrying a flower in their beaks. She wears round half-rim sunglasses with the rims on the bottom.

Her outfit consists of a collared jumper dress with a column of four rectangular buttons on the top and bottom. A prominent "FURY" logo is across her chest, split between the letters on either side of her dress. Beneath it, she wears a long-sleeve shirt with crisscrossed laces running the length of her arms. The dress ends with a semicircle opening with vertical lines on both sides of it. On the side, she has a gun holster. Her legs are exposed, but she wears knee pads with spikes on the top and bottom.
Color Schemes
Personality: Befitting her occupation as a police officer, Laem Chabang is an inquisitive and formal yet authoritarian woman. When she first meets Meryl Mei Qi to inquire about Paco Laburantes, Laem Chabang initially adopts a polite and professional demeanor. However, this is merely a facade; she possesses sharp psychological insight and quickly discards proper protocol when she senses vulnerability. Relying on the reaction from her nematodes, Laem Chabang leverages fear and intimidation to gain the upper hand, showing no hesitation in employing extreme measures once her suspicions are confirmed. Upon detecting Meryl Mei's fear, she searches the principal's computer without authorization and accuses Meryl Mei of hiding something. Once convinced that Meryl Mei is connected to Paco, she coldly instructs Ningbo to torture the civilian, permitting him to escalate the violence until they extract information. She goes as far as threatening to kill a child like Lulu if Lulu lies to her, demonstrating not only her willingness to use unethical means but also her determination to uncover the truth at any cost.

She has a cynical view of relationships and a general distrust of others, asserting that she has no boyfriend because they "always lie." A childhood incident where her teacher stole class funds and framed her for it left her bitter and obsessed with uncovering lies, viewing trusting others as a potential "pitfall." She mocks those who attempt to deceive her with a playful, callous demeanor, often giggling or repeatedly saying "no" to shut down opposition. Her short temper flares when she is frustrated, causing her to resort to screaming threats and profanity, such as holding a gun to Lulu's head.

In contrast to her usual demeanor, she is deeply affectionate and bubbly toward her partner Key West, the only person she appears to trust. She uses flirty language when texting Key, adds emojis and stickers, and playfully plans their future life together. Laem Chabang is motivated by a sense of entitlement and shared grievance with Key West, believing that they possess "talent and capabilities" that society has never properly rewarded. This perceived injustice fuels her greed, driving her to betray Hacca Howler in hopes of seizing his fortune for herself and Key. She explicitly states that the 50 billion dollars at stake "supersedes loyalty," calling it a "rule of precedence in human society."
Abilities: Stand

Lyin' Eyes allows Laem Chabang to control adrenaline-sensing nematodes that she raises as pets and keeps attached to her sunglasses. The nematodes work as a polygraph to detect if a person is being untruthful.

personagens.resumo: Ningbo (寧波(ニンポー), Ninpō) is a secondary antagonist featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands, specifically the "200 Balloons and Lyin' Eyes" story arc.

namesake.texto: Ningbo, Zhejiang, PRC (Chinese sub-provincial port city)

cod.texto: THE MATTEKUDASAI causes his gun to explode, blasting his head off

Appearance: Ningbo is a man with large, round eyes, and small irises. He is sometimes shown with very thin eyebrows, though usually appears as if he lacks them. He is bald, and wears a round fire helmet with a prominent light fixture on the front, a visor on top of it, and a neck guard in the back. The helmet has a strip that extends toward his nose, similar to a nose guard on a nasal helmet. He usually displays a sharp gaze with a neutral expression.

He is dressed in a heavy, double-breasted trench coat with wide lapels and a loose fit, giving him a bulky silhouette. The coat is secured with five circular buttons running down the front on each side, resembling screws.
Color Schemes
Personality: Ningbo is a quiet and stoic individual whose intense gaze makes him naturally intimidating, especially during interrogations. As a man of few words, Ningbo never once says his Stand name out loud, which is a trait that Paco Laburantes picks up on and taunts him about. Meryl Mei Qi assesses him to be quite crazy and someone who cares more about money than loyalty. However, she believes that Ningbo is vindictive and won't accept her bribe of sharing Howler's 50 billion dollars since he wants to avenge Bobby Jean. He shows his conviction by fighting relentlessly, refusing to back down even after receiving a nearly fatal beatdown from Paco.

He is observant, as he notices Meryl Mei quickly send a message to her students on her keyboard, and later notices when Paco enters IKO IKO. Although he follows Laem Chabang's orders, he initially voices concern about using his Stand ability on a civilian and questions how far he should go with it, suggesting that he has moral boundaries. Nonetheless, he attacks Meryl anyways, believing in his teammate's suspicions of the principal.
Abilities: Ningbo has an extremely high pain tolerance. Even after taking brutal damage from Paco, including having his teeth shattered and his head struck with a rifle so forcefully that one of his eyes bulges out, he continues standing and fighting.
Stand
200 Balloons allows Ningbo to locally inflate objects or body parts of people by touching them, causing them to swell until they burst like a balloon.

personagens.resumo: Wild Cat Size (ワイルド・キャット・サイズ, Wairudo Kyatto Saizu) is a group of secondary antagonists featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands, specifically the "Hualalai - Cat Size" story arc.

ja_kanji.texto: ワイルド・キャット・サイズ

namesake.texto: Japanese slang for strays | Cat Size (Suzi Quatro song)

Appearance: The three cats are all of the same breed with no notable differences between them. Their physical characteristics include pointed ears, light-colored eyes, and long tails that often point straight up. Their coloration closely resembles Siamese cats with the fur on their bodies being primarily light-colored, and their extremities being much darker. The pattern on their faces in particular resemble an executioner's mask with the mouth exposed.

Upon activating their Stand abilities, the cats' tails unleash several light-colored strings. When they're enraged, the cats begin to change in appearance with the wires spawning from every part of their body, their ears pinned back, and fangs fully out.
Color Schemes
Personality: Not much is known about Wild Cat Size, but Rohan considers a stray cat coming to his villa unnatural. They wander around the mansion, attacking the gang attempting to steal from Rohan.

The cats are highly intelligent, capable of considering the Stand ranges of their opponents. They also act ferociously, baring their fangs and narrowing their eyes when one of their allies is beaten. They are capable of efficiently working together to stalk and capture their prey, using their shared Stand ability to form a net out of their wires.
Abilities: Stand
All three cats share Cat Size, which produces translucent wires from their fur resembling fishing line. The wires follow a target and wrap around their limbs, constantly getting tighter.

personagens.resumo: Mundra (ムンドラー, Mundorā) is a secondary antagonist featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands, specifically the "Point Blank Seal" story arc.

namesake.texto: Mundra, Gujarat, India (Indian port town) | Mudra ("Seal" in Sanskrit)

cod.texto: Torn apart by the Light Rod Stand

mangadebut.texto: TJL Chapter 35 (Mentioned)Mentioned only | TJL Chapter 37 (1st full debut)

Appearance: Mundra is a dark-skinned man of average build with narrow eyes and a bald head. His forehead bears a tattoo of a circle with a geometric emblem resembling the Taj Mahal or Columns of Gediminas inside it. The symbol has a horizontal line at the bottom with vertical lines extending from both sides, and a line in the middle emerging from a semioval.

Mundra wears a large, light-colored hooded jacket with several spikes protruding from its hood and shoulders. The sides of his jacket has the "skull clutched by hands" imagery that is also present on his Stand. His dark pants are decorated with numerous studs in his first appearance, but the next chapter shows it decorated with overlapping circular plates instead. He wears a choker on his neck and a location-tracking anklet is fastened around one of his ankles.
Personality: Mundra is greedy and easily swayed by the prospect of wealth. Although he claims that he had not originally intended to murder the wealthy elderly woman, repeatedly hearing the dead discuss her fortune eventually tempted him to poison her for the money. His explanation suggests weak restraint and a tendency to rationalize his own wrongdoing after acting on selfish impulses.

He is also cruel and psychologically manipulative while carrying out his assignment. Through Point Blank Seal, his victims' insecurities, guilt, and trauma are used against them, though the extent to which Mundra directs the spirits of the dead is unclear. The spirits mock Jodio's childhood behavior and disorder, exploit Dragona and Paco's painful family and relationship histories, and torment Usagi as Max and Alison as her deceased husband. Mundra himself later mocks Jodio's antisocial personality disorder as Jodio leaves him behind. He continues the attack even when innocent visitors become involved, showing little concern for the harm caused as long as he can complete his assignment.

Despite his cowardly method of attacking from afar through his Stand, he also acts boldly. When his Stand is neutralized, he attempts to take Dragona hostage with a knife regardless of several police officers being nearby.

Mundra is primarily motivated by self-preservation rather than loyalty. He accepts the operation in exchange for the possibility of overturning his life sentence and repeatedly distances himself from the person directing it, insisting that he is merely a scout and prisoner rather than a trusted associate. Once captured and beaten by Team Jodio, he begs his interrogators to stop, provides information, and offers to act as an intermediary in the exchange for Tory.
Abilities: Stand

Mundra's Stand, Point Blank Seal, manifests through physical stickers. Mundra initially attaches a sticker to a target directly, after which the stickers spread like an infection to anyone who steps in a victim's blood. The stickers act as a boundary between this world and the next, allowing Mundra to remotely listen to conversations, examine the targets' thoughts and memories, and expose them to restless spirits that attack them from "point blank range."

Mundra claims that his Stand also allows him to hear the voices of the dead, which led him to hear spirits discussing the fortune of the elderly woman he later murdered. Damage inflicted upon Point Blank Seal's stickers is transferred to Mundra, and sufficiently damaging them causes the stickers attached to other targets to begin peeling away.
Weaponry
Mundra carries a small, sharply curved tactical blade resembling a karambit. He uses it to attack Dragona after the remote effects of Point Blank Seal are neutralized.

personagens.resumo: This is a list of unnamed characters found in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands. These characters play various roles throughout the story. Unnamed characters with enough notability are given their own articles, marked in blue.
This currently unnamed Stand is featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

Appearance: The Stand initially appears as two long, glowing rods. The rods can bend independently before joining together to form the outline of a simplified humanoid figure. Its body consists of a circular head, an angular torso, and two long legs, with no visible face, arms, or internal features.

During its attacks, numerous small, round protrusions can appear along portions of the Stand's outline. After killing Mundra, its humanoid form separates back into two straight rods, which ascend into the sky. The Stand can also move in its separated rod form, following Team Jodio across the roof of their vehicle before breaking through it and reforming inside.
Abilities: The exact nature, maximum range, and activation conditions of the Stand's ability are currently unknown. It is a long-distance Stand capable of pursuing and attacking targets while its user remains absent from the surrounding area. However, its ability to locate targets depends on an external surveillance system rather than its own independent detection capabilities.
Surveillance-Based Pursuit

The Stand is capable of pursuing specific targets over long distances, including through buildings and underwater. Its appearances coincide with electronic devices located near its targets, which are associated with an external surveillance system controlled by the user.

When it attacks Mundra, he is wearing an electronic ankle monitor. It later follows Team Jodio to a concealed van inside an underground parking garage and attacks their smartphones, despite them being switched off, because the group attempted to avoid electronic surveillance. After the group escapes Honolulu aboard a private submersible, a dolphin equipped with a waterproof electronic device swims near the vessel shortly before the Stand locates and attacks the vessel underwater.

During the attack on the submersible, the military's surveillance operation successfully locates the vessel using a drone launched from a naval ship. Jodio Joestar deduces that the Stand's user is monitoring their position remotely through the surveillance system, rather than the Stand independently detecting their whereabouts. He subsequently uses a speargun created by THE MATTEKUDASAI to destroy the surveillance device attached to the dolphin outside the vessel. Once the device is destroyed, the Stand loses sight of the group and withdraws, although not before launching another attack against the submersible.
Physical Attacks

The Stand's rods possess enough force to pierce through solid structures. They break through the roof of the concealed van while pursuing Team Jodio and later penetrate the hull of their submersible from underwater.

The rods can bend and combine their ends into a circular shape. The Stand can also produce numerous small protrusions along its rods, which it can shoot out as projectiles. Against Mundra, these protrusions appear along one side of its humanoid outline after one of its legs touches his leg. Numerous small holes suddenly pierce the corresponding half of Mundra's body before he is torn apart.

During the attack on the submersible, the protrusions fire multiple projectiles throughout the cabin. After losing track of Team Jodio, the Stand unleashes another barrage of projectiles that puncture the vessel's hull in numerous places, allowing seawater to flood inside.
Paco Laburantes is able to physically grab and strike the rods using The Hustle, demonstrating that the Stand itself can be directly interacted with and bent by an external force.

personagens.resumo: Doctor Roberts (ドクター・ロバーツ, Dokutā Robātsu) is a tertiary ally featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: Doctor Robert (The Beatles song)

Appearance: Doctor Roberts is an elderly adult man of average build. He has pronounced wrinkles and a tired expression, with small drooping eyes, thick eyebrows, and slightly sunken cheeks. He has short hair with long, curved bangs that fall forward along both sides of his face and a mustache.

Roberts wears a dark, wide-brimmed fedora hat with a flat top. Under a long, light lab coat that reaches his knees, he wears a buttoned shirt with dark collars, decorated with a floral pattern that extends across his torso. A lanyard with an identification card hangs from his neck. His pants are loose and he wears simple shoes.
Color Schemes
Personality: Doctor Roberts is a cautious and pragmatic physician who prefers to remain detached from matters outside his medical work. He generally behaves professionally and focuses on treating his patients rather than questioning the circumstances surrounding their injuries.

Roberts is especially reluctant to become involved in Meryl Mei Qi's personal affairs. He describes their relationship in transactional terms, repeatedly emphasizing that he only provides medical services in exchange for payment and does not want to know the details of her activities. He is similarly evasive when questioned about the exact nature of his relationship with her.

Although Roberts tries to avoid unnecessary involvement, he still helps others when they are in danger. He continues treating seriously injured patients despite the unusual circumstances surrounding them and ultimately cooperates with Team Jodio when necessary. However, he becomes anxious and irritable when others reveal information that could place him in danger or draw him further into their conflict, showing a strong concern for his own safety.
Abilities: Medical Expertise

As a physician, Doctor Roberts possesses extensive medical knowledge and surgical experience. He serves as Meryl Mei Qi's general practitioner and has previously performed cosmetic procedures for her, including a gold thread lift surgery. He is also familiar with advanced medical equipment, recognizing that the equipment Meryl acquired for treating Yokohama is comparable to that of an intensive care unit.

Roberts is capable of treating severe traumatic injuries under improvised conditions. At IKO IKO, he is tasked with reattaching the severed fingers of Meryl and Paco Laburantes. He later treats Usagi after his foot is bitten off by a lion, bringing the necessary medical tools and drugs and administering powerful medication while tending to the injury inside a concealed van.

ja_kanji.texto: バーバラ・アン・ジョースター

namesake.texto: Barbara Ann (The Regents single, later popularized by The Beach Boys)

family.texto: Joseph Joestar (Father) | Suzi Q (Mother) | Unnamed Husband | Dragona Joestar (First Child) | Jodio Joestar (Second Child) | Holy Joestar-Kira (Sister) | Yoshikage Kira (Nephew) | Kei Nijimura (Niece) See: Joestar Family

Appearance: Barbara is a thin woman of average height, with short, light, chin-length hair styled like a bob cut. She wears a polka dot sun hat, a long sleeveless vest with a polka dot pattern over a sleeveless top, and pants cropped above her ankles.

She wore various different outfits in flashbacks along with varying hair colors. Four years prior, Barbara had a hairstyle resembling a pixie cut, with side-swept bangs and shorter hair on the sides. One of her outfits was an oversized dotted T-shirt paired with a suspender dress. The T-shirt had a centered graphic saying "HAWAIIAN" on a ribbon below a circle with several palm trees inside. A few months later, she is seen with a polka dot dress. In other flashbacks, Barbara had dark hair with the chin-length bob cut style along with a headband and a T-shirt saying "Aloha". While going to work, she had a plain sunhat with a striped ribbon and a polka dot dress.
Color Schemes
Personality: Barbara is a diligent individual and although slightly strict at times, is a loving mother who thoroughly looks out for her children. She is a hard worker who takes on two jobs to support her family after her husband left home. Her day begins with a strict routine: waking up at 6:45 in the morning, starting the washing machine, then getting dressed in the bathroom. She prepares a nutritious breakfast that includes toast, fruit, ham, and eggs—fried or boiled for seven minutes—along with fried broccoli. Afterward, she wakes up her children with a good-morning kiss and hangs the laundry out to dry before catching the bus to go to work at 8:06 A.M. She staunchly refuses to accept a diagnosis of antisocial personality disorder for her son Jodio, even chiding the doctor for suggesting it. Barbara is also concerned about the company her children keep, particularly wary of influences like Paco Laburantes.

Due to her children discreetly working to maintain her well-being, everyone in the neighborhood respects and loves Barbara, providing her with assistance whenever she needs it. For instance, a neighborhood boy brings Barbara her bag if she forgets it, or another person may bring her an umbrella if it's raining while she's at the bus stop.

mangadebut.texto: TJL Chapter 8 (Mentioned)Mentioned only | TJL Chapter 33 (1st full debut)

Appearance: Alison is an adult woman with sharp, narrow eyes, thick S-shaped eyebrows, and prominent eyelashes. Her hair is spiky and light-colored, reaching her shoulders. She has bangs that hang down over her forehead over her right eye. She wears a patterned, long-sleeved dress with a floral motif across the fabric, along with layered necklaces made of large beads and segments. When she goes outside, she wears a long trenchcoat.
Personality: According to Usagi Alohaoe, Alison is a responsible parent, especially in how she cares for Tory Alohaoe in spite of the family's difficulties. Despite this, Usagi also describes his relationship with Alison as distant and strained. After his father died, Alison struggled to support the family and became increasingly focused on Tory. When Usagi was 14, he told her he had a crush on a male friend from another school. Alison reacted by sending him to a correctional facility, revealing her homophobia. Ever since that incident, she has been giving Usagi the cold shoulder, preferring to focus on her daughter.

As revealed through the Stand ability of Point Blank Seal, Alison was unfaithful toward her husband and had been secretly cheating on him with Max. After her husband's death, Alison continues to visit and rely on Max. Alison keeps her affair with Max hidden from her family, as Usagi confesses he had never heard of Max before the cyber fraud incident.

Additionally, Alison is highly gullible. When her computer displays a loud and frightening warning, Alison panics and immediately calls the fake support number shown on the screen, then follows the caller's instructions step by step. While doing so, she tries to keep Tory calm and tells her to stay seated. Although Alison is initially uneasy about the supposed support center's procedure, she ultimately trusts it and is manipulated into giving away her personal and banking information, leading to the loss of her family's assets.
