personagens.resumo: Two unnamed officers from the Honolulu Police Department are tertiary antagonists featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

Appearance: Both police officers are men with muscular builds and dark police uniforms. The uniform consists of a collared T-shirt with a chest pocket, a walkie-talkie attached to their left shoulders, wristbands, a gun belt with a holster, and pants. Their shirts have the Honolulu Police Department insignia on their chest pocket and shoulder patches. The back of their shirts have "POLICE" centered at the top in large letters.
One of the officers has short, light, side-swept hair that is trimmed a bit on the sides. He is overweight with a double chin, has thick eyebrows, and a horseshoe mustache.
The other officer has short, dark hair in a flattop style that is closely trimmed on the sides and back. He wears dark sunglasses.
Color Schemes
Personality: The two Honolulu police officers are immoral, lack integrity, and have superiority complexes. The one with light-colored hair disregards the concerns of the individuals he's interrogating. He uses his authority to intimidate and manipulate situations to his advantage. For example, when Dragona doesn't want the officer's face to get too close because of health concerns of COVID-19, the officer twists the situation to be an attack on his race because of his fair skin in contrast to Dragona's dark skin. He is extremely perverted, using his routine procedure to pull over vehicles if they suspect unlawful behavior as a pretext for inappropriate behavior. He's quick to impose accusations without substantial evidence, implying theft without proper justification. The officer is also implied to be bisexual, as he gets more aroused upon noticing that Dragona has male genitals and says he dreams about Dragona every night after the incident. Moreover, he is even a pedophile as he describes his intention of wanting to molest Jodio.

The second officer is passive about his partner's behavior, enabling him by not intervening. He turns a blind eye to what his partner is doing, mockingly asking whether his partner will be okay on his own with a chuckle while seeing him assault Dragona. He gets aggressive when Jodio exits the car, immediately pointing his gun at the minor.

personagens.resumo: An unnamed watch salesman who appears as a tertiary antagonist featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

Appearance: The watch salesman has a dark Fu Manchu mustache and short light-colored hair combed to the side. He is impeccably dressed in a tailored suit with a distinctive spotty pattern on his tie.
Color Schemes
Personality: The watch salesman is initially introduced as a warm and welcoming host, politely welcoming Dragona and Usagi and offering to showcase them a selection of high-class watches. The clerk demonstrates a sales acumen, seizing opportunities to upsell and elaborately describe the exclusivity and value of the store's items. He only starts to take a keen interest in the pair after he notices a large diamond in Dragona's possession. He leads them to a private room in the back and goes above and beyond by offering to serve them beverages and alcohol to please them.

He is also an observant man, as he notices Dragona and Usagi's nervousness and begins to suspect them, but still acts patiently to correct Usagi's misunderstandings. He shows his assertive and meticulous side when he notices that one of the watches on the table is missing. His gracious demeanor shifts into a stern and watchful gaze, discreetly signaling security and warning the two that there are surveillance cameras watching them. Despite thinking that they're thieves, the clerk initially still speaks respectfully toward them. However, he has a no-nonsense attitude and quickly gets agitated, insulting them as petty crooks and threatening to call the police.

The clerk is diligent, having a strong sense of responsibility toward both his family and his company's reputation. Upon realizing he wrongfully accused his customers, he profoundly apologizes and feels shameful for his mistake.

Nonetheless, she is focused on ensuring that the corrections are completed before the chapter begins distribution and accepts the manuscript despite Rohan's unusual insistence on using only analog methods.

She is familiar enough with Rohan to question his decisions directly, but remains composed when faced with his abrupt behavior and rudeness. When assigning the last-minute revisions, Rohan flatters her by calling her a first-rate manga editor, wanting to persuade her to accept the task despite the strict deadline.

Laura wears a United States Marine Corps uniform decorated with several ribbons and insignia across the chest, along with a military cap. She also wears earrings.

personagens.resumo: An unnamed girl who appears as a tertiary antagonist featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

Appearance: She is a young woman with shoulder-length hair styled with four tied-back sections, having two ponytails on each side. In gym class while playing volleyball, she wears a light swimsuit with dark edges. A dark diamond with a light hand symbol is centered on the chest.
While on the school bus, she wears a light collared long sleeve dress with two buttons on the top and a dark belt around her waist. She also has dark sneakers on.

Personality: The girl initially presents herself as kind and caring to Dragona, offering encouragement and support during gym class. However, this facade quickly fades after Dragona accidentally hits her face with a volleyball, revealing her violent personality and deep-seated hatred toward Dragona.

During school, she repeatedly intimidates and abuses Dragona, both physically and emotionally, due to the latter's weak and girlish mannerisms. This culminates with her ganging up on Dragona on the bus, making derogatory comments, questioning Dragona's gender, and sexually assaulting Dragona. She goes as far as to attempt to humiliate Dragona by undressing Dragona in front of all of their classmates, chastising Dragona for not wearing a bra, and attempting to emasculate Dragona by "drawing" one using an eyelash curler.
Despite her abhorrent behavior, she seems to be well-liked by her peers and seemingly even the school faculty, likely due in part to her family's wealth and their donations to the school.

Appearance: Latrato is a man with long, dark hair styled in a slick, wavy, swept-back manner. He has a slightly muscular build, a wide nose, and a light mustache.

When he first arrived at Hawaii, he wore a sailor hat, hoodie, and pants with rolled up cuffs. Later, he is shown with a long sleeve shirt. In another appearance, he wears a wide-brimmed hat. In another photo, he wears a beanie and his sideburns resemble a lightning strike.

He is also resourceful and intuitive in regards to working with land. Instead of building vertical wells, he deduces there must be rain water accumulating in the gaps between the volcanic rocks. Accordingly, he devises a strategy to dig tunnels horizontally into the slope of the mountain instead.

Appearance: Hacca's grandfather is an elderly man with a broad face, a Fu Manchu mustache, and a muscular build. His head is shaved on the sides with a short bowl cut hairstyle. He often wears Hawaiian clothing, such as a suit with a floral-patterned turtleneck underneath. When killing Monte Brutto, he wears a hoodie. When he is watching TV with his grandson, he wears a loose-fitting T-shirt, shorts, slippers, and a floral lei around his neck.

He has a strong sense of personal honor, willing to take extreme measures to protect what he believes belongs to his family. After assassinating Monte Brutto, he also murders the man's driver so that there would be no witnesses to his crime, though he apologizes for having to do so.

Howler is shown to be gentle with his family, particularly his grandson, Hacca. He teaches Hacca about their heritage, emphasizing the importance of respecting their family's history and heirlooms. Howler is also practical and forward-thinking, recognizing the changing times with the rise of digital records. Despite having the mindset that nothing in the world lasts forever, he secures his family's future by legally registering their land to protect it from future disputes.

Despite his negative traits and abusive nature, he shows brief moments of affection by promising to take Paco out to go fishing with him. personagens.resumo: Pink Dark Boy (ピンクダークの少年, Pinku Dāku no Shōnen), or simply Pink Dark (ピンクダーク, Pinku Dāku), is the titular protagonist of Rohan Kishibe's horror-suspense manga, Pink Dark Boy.

In the Rohan au Louvre film, Pink Dark wears a buttoned tuxedo, checkerboard tie, and a bowler hat with the checkerboard pattern. He also wields a cane with a diamond inside. In Rohan au Louvre, a page of Pink Dark attempting to comfort a crying girl is seen. Based on Rohan Kishibe's experiences with Nanase Fujikura, Pink Dark is portrayed as having a gentle side and a desire to help others.
In "Bloodsoaked Bookmark," Rohan's work is said to be so impactful that when Pink Dark faces a horrific enemy, the reader's skin crawls.

Pages from the TV drama and Rohan au Louvre film portray Pink Dark as a brave, enigmatic figure, guided by the wind and reserved to himself. He primarily operates on logic and reason, opposing needless violence and avoiding risks. However, he also displays empathy for strangers.
Abilities: Pink Dark Boy's abilities are mostly unknown. He is shown fighting both unarmed and with various weapons, including a sword when facing Hot Summer Martha. He has also been depicted wielding a bow and arrow.
Time Erasure

In Volume 15 of Pink Dark Boy, Pink Dark is said to "blow away time"時間をブッ飛ばす. Jodio considers the scene, which appears on page 92 of the volume, to be his favorite in the series. The exact nature and mechanics of this ability are unknown.
